newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials surge to another record high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials surge to another record high.

text.p: Zimbabwe's key industrial share index surged over 93 points to yet another record high on Monday as many local investors continued to flee low short-term interest rates on the local money market, brokers said.
"There is quite some pressure on the (share) market. A lot of brokers are holding buy orders, and many of these are from people moving out of the money market," one dealer said.
Interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market have fallen to around 18 percent from about 30 percent in January, and are expected to stay low in 1997.
"It's the main reason why we have this uncharacteristic pressure for this time of the year," the dealer added.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's (ZSE) 57-counter industrial index jumped 93.15 points to a record 8,709.65 following some big gains in several heavyweights, including bluechip conglomerate Delta, which traded 100 cents higher at 3,800, and banking group Barclays -- which also traded 100 cents up at 2,500.

Many share market analysts expect the ZSE to remain firm for at least another three months amid predictions that Zimbabwe's agriculture-based economy will grow by up to seven percent in 1997 from an estimated five percent in 1996.
But the current pressure on industrial shares does not extend to the ZSE's secondary minings portfolio, which analysts say traditionally enjoys the support of very few corporate local investors.
The seven-share mining index lost 5.06 points in quiet trade on Monday to end at 1,061.94, dragged largely by nickel producer Bindura which traded 10 cents down at 750.
